summary: Round-3 verify. Both round-1 test minors are measured dead, not merely edited. Ten mutations run against CommitLog.java, each restored and the worktree confirmed byte-identical after every one: dropping the .delta suffix and unpadding the SEQUENCE are now both killed, and killed specifically by theKeyCarriesTheEpochZeroPaddedSoLexicographicOrderIsNumericOrder, the test whose name claims the key grammar. recover() with an empty body is now killed by twoEpochsWriteToDisjointPrefixesAndNeitherSeesTheOthersDeltas via the new positive control, and the restructured test still kills what it killed before -- recover() listing across all epochs, and logPrefix() ignoring the epoch. All 16 CommitLogTest tests were checked for individual discrimination; 15 of 16 kill a mutation no sibling kills. Suite 490 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. check-tdd green (7 new tests, red records at the current file hash b66f34f7, spot-checked in red.log: every one fails at a line in the final file, and the two-arg-constructor test's initial pass-against-skeleton is visible in the log exactly as the backlog row describes). check-test-integrity green; the test diff is pure addition with zero removed or loosened lines, so no assertion was weakened alongside the production change. No findings.
notes: Mutations killed (each verified by parsing the JUnit XML for the killing test name, not by exit code): keyFor drops .delta -> theKeyCarries...; keyFor renders sequence unpadded -> theKeyCarries...; recover() body emptied -> twoEpochsWrite..., recoveryRebuildsOffsetsFromTheLogAlone, aFencedWritersLaterPut...; recover() lists prefix+/ctl/log/0/ across all epochs -> twoEpochsWrite..., aFencedWritersLaterPut...; logPrefix() renders constant 0 instead of epoch -> twoEpochsWrite..., epochPrefixesSort..., theKeyCarries..., aFencedWritersLaterPut...; two-arg constructor delegates to epoch 1 -> theTwoArgConstructor..., theChainReports...; epoch() returns constant 0 -> theChainReports...; epoch<0 relaxed to epoch<-1 -> aNegativeEpochIsRefused; epoch padded to %08x -> theKeyCarries...; epoch unpadded %x -> epochPrefixesSort..., theKeyCarries....

Observation, not a finding: epochPrefixesSortInNumericOrderAcrossTheNineToSixteenBoundary is mutation-subsumed by theKeyCarriesTheEpochZeroPaddedSoLexicographicOrderIsNumericOrder -- the %08x mutation survives it while theKeyCarries kills it, and no mutation was found that only epochPrefixesSort kills. It is retained deliberately: it asserts the ORDERING property in the form the reader depends on, where theKeyCarries asserts a literal string that happens to have it. Keeping it is right; it is a documented reason, not dead weight, and it is not redundant in the sense that matters (it would survive a future rewrite of the literal).

The positive control did NOT make any sibling redundant. Its kill (recover() emptied) is shared with recoveryRebuildsOffsetsFromTheLogAlone, but its purpose is local integrity -- it stops THIS test being green because nothing is seen at all -- and that is exactly what the empty-recover mutation now proves.

The red for twoEpochsWrite... in the final recording is at line 278, the positive control itself. Genuine red, and worth stating plainly: the negative fencing assertions at 282/285 were never observed red against the stub, because the control fires first. Mutation testing covers that gap here -- both negatives are shown load-bearing by the list-all-epochs and ignore-epoch mutations -- which is the stronger evidence, so this is stated for the record rather than as a defect.

Backlog row M4.4 is honest. Every claim in it that is checkable was checked: 490 tests, both round-1 test findings stated in the terms they were found in, the M4.4b major given its own row with an owner rather than absorbed, and the 'one test initially passed against the skeleton' claim visible in .harness/tdd/red.log (theTwoArgConstructor... is invoked at 62392 with no FAILED, and FAILS later at 62664 against the corrected stub).

On the production reviewer's remaining minor (CommitLog.java javadoc says 'carried as its own backlog row' without naming M4.4b): recording rather than fixing is right, and I agree. The pointer is not lost -- CommitLogTest.java:247 names M4.4b in an as() description, and the M4.4b row itself opens 'Found by round-1 review of M4.4' -- so a reader has a path in both directions. Fixing it would change the bytes, invalidate both verdicts and open a fourth round whose entire surface is the prose the fix just added, which is the spiral review.md rule 11 exists to stop. It is a comment-completeness nit with no effect on falsifiability.
